title: Heavy, dense bread, undercooked crusts
text:
Heavy, dense bread, undercooked crusts. I love homemade bread and have been making all our bread for several years now. I started with a sub-fifty dollar machine and upgraded to a very fancy, high end bread machine. I still use my inexpensive first unit the most often actually. This unit is my 3rd bread maker and its definitely running third place to the others.

We made 4 different loaves over the last two days using 3 recipes - all ended with subpar results each time. The crusts were always too light on each setting and the light crust setting loaf wasn't completely cooked. One of the other loaves never rose fully - that could have been the yeast quality/quantity or the bread machine, I'm not sure.

I'm using tried and true recipes that we know make light, delicious breads and fresh ingredients including King Arthur bread flour. All four loaves were very, very dense and chewy. They reminded me of bagels in texture and chewiness. The double kneading wands create a dual ball of dough and I suspect that has something to do with the thick, heavy end product.

I'm going to fiddle with my recipes a bit and try this machine a few more times because there are several things to like about it. I like the large numbers and buttons on the front face - very easy to see. I also like that this machine puts out less direct heat while cooking than my other two. Its better insulated and the heat stays primarily inside where it should be.
